pollution noun

also polluted, pollute, air pollution, smog

modern

M-O s.v. pollution, citing Egger: inquinātiōne āëris

inquinātiō, inquinātiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

Lewis & Short has the noun only in the Vulgate (Sap. 14.26), of the defiling of souls; the modern sense rests on the classical verb.

Other words

  • inquinō, inquināre, inquināvī, inquinātum — befoul, pollute

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Ov. M. 14.56: venēnīs, of poisoning a pool (Lewis & Short); Hor. S. 1.8.37 (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    The classical way to say it: āēr inquinātus, aqua inquināta. Also figurative, to stain a reputation (Cic.).

  • pollūtiō, pollūtiōnis f. — defilement

    noun, third declension · avoid · late Latin · Pall. 9.10; Vulg. Judith 13.20 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Late Latin, and in Christian authors of moral or ritual defilement; use inquinātiō.

Examples

  • oleam quam prīmum ex terrā tollitō. sī inquināta erit, lavātō ā foliīs et stercore pūrgātō

    pick the olives up off the ground at once; if they are dirty, wash them and clean off the leaves and muckCato Agr. 65.1

See also dirt.
